newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian minority parties attack poll funding.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian minority parties attack poll funding.

text.p: Indonesia's minority parties said on Monday that election funding given by the government was too small to cover campaign costs for the country's May polls.

Ismail Hasan Metareum, head of the Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP), was quoted by the official Antara news agency as saying that the government election funding of 500 million rupiah ($208,000) was not enough.
The funds make up most of the minority parties' income.

"According to our estimates what is needed is two or three billion rupiah or at the least one billion rupiah and if it was very economical 750 million. This assistance of 500 million rupiah is, of course, not enough," Metareum said.
He said his party must look for alternative sources of funding for the May 29 election, without giving details.

Surjadi, leader of the government-backed faction of the divided Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI), said the 500 million rupiah would not pay for the cost of the four week campaign, which begins officially on April 27 and ends on May 23.
He said the money had to be split between the PDI's 302 branches.
Information Minister Harmoko, head of the ruling Golkar party, declined to comment on the funding issue.
The minority parties have long complained that Golkar, whose leaders are drawn from senior government figures and business executives, has no problem funding its extensive activities.

Under Indonesia's tightly controlled electoral system, Golkar is nearly assured of a landslide victory in the polls and is expected to reach its target of more than 70 percent of the vote, up from around 68 percent at the last poll.
Public rallies have been banned for the election and the government wants to restrict campaigning to television debates.
Interior Minister Yogie Memet on Monday recognised the funding was less than the parties needed but said it was twice that given to them at the last election in 1992.

"However, this is the amount that can be given by the government because every expenditure must be in line with the financial abilities of the state," Memet said, adding the parties could look for funding from other sources.
Even before the start of the official campaign period, bright yellow Golkar flags can be seen throughout Central Java province. Party members have also hosted pop music concerts.
PPP supporters in the Central Java town of Yogyakarta have countered with unsanctioned motorcycle rallies every Sunday.
